review: The hymn is Psalm 46:2 with Hebrews 4:15–16 and 1 Corinthians 10:13: 1:1–4 is Ps 46:2 (אֱלֹהִים לָנוּ מַחֲסֶה וָעֹז) with Phil 4:6, 2:1–4 1 Cor 10:13 with Ps 50:15, 3:1–4 Heb 4:16 (כִּסֵּא הַחֶסֶד) with Rom 8:34, 4:1–4 Heb 4:15, 5:1–4 1 Thess 1:10, and 6:1–4 1 Thess 4:17 with Rev 21:4.

1:1 אֱלֹהִים מַחֲסֶה־לָּנוּ — the psalm's own order is אֱלֹהִים לָנוּ מַחֲסֶה; the Hebrew moves לָּנוּ to the end of the compound so that the line keeps the printed eight syllables and the stanza's first word is still אֱלֹהִים.

2:2 דֶּרֶךְ לָצֵאת יַרְאֵנוּ — the Arabic فَمَعهَا يُعْطِينَا عَزَا is 'with it He gives us consolation', but the verse behind the hymn is 1 Cor 10:13's ἔκβασιν, the way out; the Hebrew keeps the way out (דֶּרֶךְ לָצֵאת) because the next stanza turns to the throne of grace and the two together are the argument.

3:2 בְּלֵב בָּנִים וּבְבִטְחָה — the Arabic بِثِقَةِ الْبَنِين is 'with the confidence of sons'; the Hebrew keeps both nouns and lets בְּלֵב carry the filial relation, since a literal בְּבִטְחַת בָּנִים would be nine syllables and the line has to end on the confidence.

5:4 מִן־הַחֵמָה הַבָּאָה — the Arabic سَنَخْلُصُ مِنَ الْغَضَب is 'we shall be saved from the wrath'; the Hebrew uses the fixed phrase of 1 Thess 1:10 (מִן־הַחֵמָה הַבָּאָה), so the line names the eschatological wrath and not a general anger.
